# Mathematical notes on scans 113–128

## What the pages do

**M1 · Scan 113.** The opening continues an argument in group-theoretic terms. The orders written over the three rotations \(\rho_0,\rho_1,\rho_\infty\) are \(n,2,3\). The stabilizer at \(s_0\) is generated by \(\rho_0\). Choosing a reflection exchanging \(s_0,t_0\) leads to the membership condition in (34′). The definitions behind (34) begin before this batch.

**M2 · Scans 114–115.** Given \(\lambda\in Z'\), (35) constructs an edge \(\{s,\lambda t\}\) from an old edge \(\{s,t\}\). Relations (36) and (37) compare the two stars at the same vertex. Their equal sizes give the same vertex order. The action of \(G_0^+\) on oriented edges is transported to the new graph \(\Gamma_\lambda\).

**M3 · Scans 115–116.** Axiom \(T_0\,4\), labelled (38), recovers triangular faces from their three edges. The « icosaèdre gauche » shows the problem with inferring the face set from the graph alone. Its graph has six vertices and fifteen edges, but only half the twenty vertex triples are faces. The digression (39) asks for two common neighbors for each edge (A1), and a connected, nonempty graph of neighbors at each vertex (A2).

**M4 · Scans 117–119.** Substitution of \(v=\lambda u\) translates A1 into the intersection-size condition (40). The analogous connectivity question survives the bijection of stars. Axiom \(T_0\,5\) in (41) asks for a graph isomorphism, and (42) writes the condition on its vertex permutation. The next page writes down the resulting polyhedron \(P_\lambda\) and imposes \(T_0\,6\) so that \(Z'\) commutes with all of \(G_0\).

**M5 · Scans 119–121.** There is a canonical injection \(G_0\longrightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(P_\lambda)\). The argument on scan 120 compares the stabilizer of an oriented edge with the stabilizer of a flag. It concludes that the groups are isomorphic in (43). The restriction to \(G_0^+\) and \(G_\lambda^+\) is displayed separately in (44) with a question mark. The discussion of index-two subgroups distinguishes odd from even vertex order.

**M6 · Scans 121–122.** He provisionally calls the structures satisfying \(T_0\,1\) through \(T_0\,6\) « spéciales ». Formula (45) defines equivalence on structures carried by the same vertex set. The prose discusses symmetry, reflexivity and transitivity. Members of an equivalence class \(\Pi\) have the common automorphism group (46). Its centralizer \(Z'\), written as a commutant in (47), acts transitively on \(\Pi\).

**M7 · Scans 123–124.** The proposed commutativity of \(Z'\) in (48) is tested by comparing \(\lambda\mu\) and \(\mu\lambda\) on edges. The diagram yields equality of their stars at each vertex. He discusses when equal stars determine the vertex, then treats the double pyramid and octahedron separately. Statement (49) gives the equal-order case and identifies the central involution in the octahedral case with the antipodism.

**M8 · Scans 125–126.** Formula (50) tests which elements fix one structure in \(\Pi\). It leads first to membership in the centre of \(G_0\), then to the equality of stars in (51). This gives the torsor conclusion subject to the stated exception. Scan 126 discusses two polygonal structures on the same set \(E\) and describes the multiplier \(n/2-1\). He then sets aside the double pyramid apart from the octahedron.

**M9 · Scans 126–127.** A permutation carrying one member of \(\Pi\) to another preserves the whole class. Formula (53) defines \(G\) from that property. The chain beginning at (54) identifies \(G_0\) with the stabilizer and kernel, embeds \(G/G_0\) in the permutations of \(\Pi\), and gives the action on \(Z'\). Formula (57) expresses the resulting affine action.

**M10 · Scan 128.** He notes \(Z'\subset G\). Applying \(\lambda\) to both endpoints gives the \(\lambda^2\) in (59), with separate captions for transport of structure and the action defined in (45). He introduces the additional condition \(T_0\,7\) that \(Z'\) be central in \(G\), relates it to an action by translations, and writes the homomorphism \(\delta:G\to Z'\) in (61). The promised canonical exact sequence begins beyond the end of this batch.

## Questions and conjectures

- **115–116.** « J'ignore, s'il existe … » asks for an orientable example not determined by its graph. His subsequent example is expressly « régulier, mais pas orientable ».
- **117–118.** « on peut se poser la question si » \(A_\lambda\) gives a graph satisfying A1 and A2. The renewed question « pourquoi cette relation … serait elle “connexe” ? » motivates \(T_0\,5\).
- **119–120.** « J'aimerais vérifier » introduces the surjectivity problem for the injection into \(\operatorname{Aut}(P_\lambda)\). He gives an argument on the next page.
- **120–121.** The question mark in (44) concerns compatibility with orientation. « donc la question est si \(\rho_1^r\) … conserve l'orientation » and « il faudra revenir là-dessus » locate exactly where the even case is left.
- **123–124.** « la relation plausible » is the assertion that \(Z'\) is commutative. He first considers imposing it as an axiom, then presents an argument from equality of stars and exceptions. The diagonal remarks qualify this argument.

## Remarks of the model

**R1 · Scan 116 · Model, high confidence.** The numbers in the « icosaèdre gauche » paragraph pass a counting check. A six-element set has 15 two-element subsets and 20 three-element subsets. Half the latter is 10. The check concerns these counts.

**R2 · Scans 124–126 · Model, low confidence about the scope of the claim.** Scan 126 places « \(n\) pair \(\geqslant6\) » by the assertion about two elements, while an interline correction later in the paragraph gives \(n\equiv0\ (4)\) and \(\geqslant8\). The multiplier written there is \(n/2-1\). As a check on its interpretation as a permutation of residues, testing \(n=6,8,10,12\) gives image sizes \(3,8,5,12\), respectively. For 6 and 10 the multiplier visits only half the residue classes. The scope of the handwritten correction is unsettled.

**R3 · Scans 120–121 · Model, high confidence as a reading of the argument.** The isomorphism line on 120 and the restriction to the plus subgroups are distinct assertions. The question mark belongs to the restriction. The marginal « il faudra revenir là-dessus » follows the discussion of that same distinction on 121.

**R4 · Reading questions · Model, low confidence.** On scan 113, in the final line below (34′), the frozen text has `\operatorname{Norm}_{\deleted{\unsure{G_0^+}}}`. The alternative is a live subscript \(G_0^+\). The small oval over the group label could be a cancellation or an emphatic retracing. On scan 124, near the end of the lower oblique note, the frozen text reads `ne correspond \unsure{,|qu'}à une structure`. Another reading is « ne correspond à une structure … que si », with no comma or intervening word. A diagonal stroke belongs to the intersecting main paragraph. The intended attachment is uncertain.
